nodes.name: American beech
nodes.desc: A common hardwood of the northern forest on the lower slopes. Its nuts are an autumn food for bears, deer and small mammals.

nodes.name: Yellow birch
nodes.desc: A major tree of the Green Mountains hardwood forest. Browsed by deer and eaten by beavers, porcupines and red squirrels.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: A conifer of the cooler, higher slopes. Beavers, deer and red squirrels are recorded feeding on it.

nodes.name: Striped maple
nodes.desc: A small understory tree whose twigs and leaves are browsed by moose and deer.

nodes.name: Bluebead
nodes.desc: A woodland wildflower of the forest floor in cool northern woods. Deer are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: The most recorded large herbivore near the forest. It browses twigs, buds and herbs and eats beechnuts.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: A large browser of young hardwood growth. Winter ticks have caused many moose deaths in Vermont in recent years.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Cuts trees to build dams, and the ponds it makes create wetland habitat for many other species.

nodes.name: North American porcupine
nodes.desc: A slow tree-climbing herbivore that eats bark and leaves of hardwoods and conifers.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: A small forest squirrel that feeds on conifer seeds, buds and bark, and is prey for many carnivores.

nodes.name: Eastern chipmunk
nodes.desc: A ground-dwelling omnivore eating nuts, seeds and some invertebrates, and is prey for foxes, bobcats and coyotes.

nodes.name: Meadow vole
nodes.desc: A small grazer of clearings and wet meadows that feeds many predators.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A small canid hunting voles and squirrels, and scavenging carrion in winter.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: A flexible omnivore that takes small mammals and carrion in the forest edge and near streams.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A large scavenging bird that feeds on carcasses of deer and moose through winter.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: The main wild canid predator of the region. It takes small mammals and deer and also scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A secretive cat that hunts squirrels, voles and hares and sometimes deer in the forest.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore feeding on beechnuts, berries, insects and carrion, and occasionally on calves or fawns.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth of the canopy and understory plants in the short northern summer.

nodes.name: Snow and cold winters
nodes.desc: Deep snow and cold shape winter foraging, and heavy snowfall on the high peaks feeds streams in spring.

nodes.name: Rain and streams
nodes.desc: Abundant precipitation feeds the mountain streams, beaver ponds and forest wetlands.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and rich soils on the slopes hold the nutrients that trees and wildflowers draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dead wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
